_meta.note: Entirely fictional fixture: a toy convergence theorem for a damped iteration. It carries no research content.

steps.title: Convergence of the damped iteration
steps.statement: If f is a q-contraction on [0,1] and step sizes h_n lie in [0,1] with every block of m steps summing to at least delta, then x_{n+1}=(1-h_n)x_n+h_n f(x_n) converges to the fixed point.

steps.title: Setting and the fixed point
steps.statement: A q-contraction on [0,1] has a unique fixed point x*.

steps.title: One-step contraction
steps.why_tier: Routine estimate; the damping is what is specific to this iteration.

steps.title: Product bound
steps.statement: A product of factors 1-a_n with a_n in [0,1] is at most exp(-sum a_n).

steps.title: Block-sum lemma
steps.statement: If every block of m consecutive steps has h-sum at least delta, the product of the block factors is at most exp(-(1-q)delta) per block, so the product tends to 0.
steps.role: replaces the usual divergent-sum condition by a block condition that tolerates vanishing steps
steps.why_tier: Without it the theorem needs sum h_n = infinity with h_n bounded below on a tail; the paper claims the block form is new.
seeds: blocks that straddle the start index
delta close to 0 and m large

steps.title: Conclusion
steps.statement: Combine S2 and S4: |x_n - x*| tends to 0.

steps.title: Remark: a rate for h_n = 1/n
steps.statement: A polynomial rate follows when h_n = 1/n.
